visible_observation: The composition relies on a single, heavy diagonal zigzag line that cuts from the bottom-left to the top-right, physically slicing through the primary headline text ('ONE SPARK IS ENOUGH'). The headline is left-aligned and stacked, while the secondary text ('Check conditions...') is entirely absent from the visual field.
critique: The layout fails to establish a clear visual hierarchy because the graphic element (the fire line) aggressively competes with the headline for dominance. By cutting through the text, the line creates visual noise that disrupts the reading path, making the poster feel chaotic rather than urgent. Furthermore, the absence of the required secondary text leaves the bottom-right quadrant as a 'dead zone' of negative space, causing the composition to feel top-heavy and unbalanced.
revision: 1. Shift the headline text to the upper-left quadrant and reduce the scale of the fire line so it acts as a framing device rather than an obstruction, ensuring the text sits clearly on the dark background. 2. Introduce the missing secondary text ('Check conditions. Extinguish completely. Protect the wild.') in the bottom-right corner to anchor the composition and balance the visual weight of the headline.
protected_strength: The high-contrast color palette (white text against deep navy) and the glowing gradient of the fire line are effective visual assets that create the necessary sense of urgency and should be preserved.
